subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this exact trusted-source matrix and require a separate explicit acknowledgement for every first install from arbitrary executable sources, including existing noninteractive and chat workflows?
rationale: The code can prove consistent enforcement and safe rendering, but only maintainers can decide which registries/catalogs constitute trusted provenance and whether the resulting compatibility break is acceptable.

options.title: Approve the strict trust gate
options.body: Accept ClawHub, bundled metadata, and official catalog mappings as trusted while requiring the dedicated acknowledgement for all other direct first installs.

options.title: Preserve unattended compatibility
options.body: Keep existing noninteractive behavior by default and expose the stricter provenance gate as an explicit opt-in policy until a migration window is complete.

options.title: Narrow the exemptions
options.body: Require acknowledgement for additional sources such as ClawHub or official catalog packages instead of treating their metadata as sufficient trust.

recommendation.title: Approve the strict trust gate
recommendation.body: Accept ClawHub, bundled metadata, and official catalog mappings as trusted while requiring the dedicated acknowledgement for all other direct first installs.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history across plugin installation, safety policy, chat installs, and CLI runner ownership points to this person for the cross-surface decision.
